title: Introduction to Philosophy
location: CSP Learning Center, 45 Ward Place, Colombo 07
description: This course is where most people start: a guided tour through the biggest questions philosophy asks, and the different ways thinkers have tried to answer them.
Across eight weeks, we cover knowledge, ethics, mind, and meaning — not as separate boxes, but as questions that connect to how you actually think and live. No prior background is expected.
Each week pairs a short reading with a live discussion, so you're not just absorbing ideas but testing them against other people's thinking.

title: Ethics in the Modern World
location: CSP Learning Center, 45 Ward Place, Colombo 07
description: What do we owe each other? This course works through the major ethical frameworks — consequences, duty, character, care — and applies them to problems people actually face today.
Expect case studies drawn from everyday life in Sri Lanka and beyond: fairness at work, family obligation, and the small decisions that add up to a life.
By the end, you won't have one tidy answer to "what's right" — but you'll have sharper tools for working it out.

title: Political Philosophy
description: Why do we accept some authority as legitimate and reject other kinds? This course traces the major arguments about the state, justice, and collective life.
We read across traditions — not just the usual Western canon — and connect the arguments to real questions about governance, rights, and civic life in Sri Lanka today.
No political affiliation assumed or required. The goal is to think more carefully, not to arrive at a party line.

title: Philosophy of Mind
location: CSP Learning Center, 45 Ward Place, Colombo 07
description: Is the mind the same thing as the brain? What makes you the same person you were ten years ago? This course takes on the oldest and strangest questions in philosophy.
We'll draw on both classic philosophical arguments and current findings from cognitive science, without assuming a science background.
Fair warning: several sessions in, most students start finding this course's questions hard to stop thinking about.

title: Logic and Critical Thinking
description: A practical course: how to spot a bad argument, build a good one, and tell the difference under pressure.
We cover the basics of formal and informal logic, common fallacies, and how bias quietly shapes reasoning — including our own.
Useful well beyond philosophy: for work, debate, and the everyday task of deciding what to believe.

title: Philosophy in Everyday Life
summary: Ideas for a more meaningful life.
location: CSP Community Room, Barnes Place, Colombo 07
description: The shortest and most applied of our courses: how philosophical ideas show up in ordinary decisions, routines, and relationships.
Drawing on Stoic, Buddhist, and existentialist ideas, we look at practical questions — how to handle a bad day, what habits are worth keeping, what "a good life" might mean for you specifically.
No essays, no exams — just structured conversation and a few short readings each week.
